extracted.intended_audience: ICML reviewers (program committee members, area chairs, external reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing reviews of submissions to the ICML conference: how to summarize claims, list merits, justify recommendations, and provide detailed constructive comments across criteria such as significance, novelty, technical quality, presentation, and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent of the review process is twofold: (1) to identify papers which offer significant contributions to the field of machine learning for attendees and readers, and (2) to provide constructive feedback to authors that they can use to improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, always think about both goals. Your role is critical to identifying impactful work and helping authors improve. Use this dual purpose to structure your review: an evaluative judgment for meta-reviewers and constructive suggestions for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term impact and high-level ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a paper, always think about the impact the work may have on the community in the long run — out-of-the-box ideas, novel problems and 'bridging fields' contributions are crucial for the successful development of the field so do not neglect high-level picture in favor of technical correctness, which is also important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give weight to novelty, problem formulation, and potential to open new research directions, not only to immediate technical correctness or incremental empirical improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware bias against novel or interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel and/or interdisciplinary works (e.g., which are not incremental extensions of previously studied problems but instead perhaps formulate a new problem of interest) are often very easy to criticize ... However, such work may be of high importance for the progress of the field in the long run, so please try to be aware of this bias, and avoid dismissive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dismissing papers solely because their assumptions or models are not yet widely accepted; be cautious about over-penalizing novelty. When criticizing, explain specific issues and suggest constructive directions rather than blanket rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of main claim(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your review begins with a summary of the main ideas of the submission. Although this part of the review may not provide much new information to authors, it is invaluable to the meta-reviewers and program chairs, and it can help the authors determine whether there are misunderstandings that need to be addressed in their author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be brief but specific. Use this section to certify you understood the submission; concise summaries help meta-reviewers and reveal misunderstandings early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits of the paper (list contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the main contributions of the paper. Contributions may be theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, connecting ideas in disparate fields ('bridge papers'), formulating a novel problem or providing a critical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to identify at least one contribution, even if modest (e.g., 'combines models in [A] and [B]'). Evaluate the significance of each listed contribution (e.g., how likely others will build on it). Use examples (experimental validation, improved complexity, robust methods, unifying frameworks, exposing limitations, novel problem formulation) to motivate your judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how strong this paper is, weighing its strengths against any potential flaws. Your evaluation should reflect absolute judgments of the contributions made by each paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume you received an unbiased sample of papers and do not adjust answers to achieve an artificial balance of positive and negative recommendations across your batch. Refer to prior ICML proceedings for typical levels of acceptability if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of your recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Write concrete arguments that explain why you gave a particular recommendation to the submission. Your arguments should be objective, specific, concise and polite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague, subjective complaints and personal-interest statements. For each argument, briefly explain its significance. If asserting prior work or that something has been done before, provide relevant citations. If an argument requires a long explanation, note it here and provide the full justification in Detailed Comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed comments for authors (top-down)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed feedback in a top-down manner, starting from the most important aspects. Use this section to support and justify the claims made in the Justification section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the most significant issues first (e.g., fatal flaws or major missing comparisons), then list less critical but useful suggestions (missing references, presentation, typos). Include concrete constructive suggestions that could help improve the work or its presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether results are important: are others likely to use or build on the ideas? Does the submission address a difficult task in a better way than previous work? Does it advance the state of the art or provide unique data/conclusions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer questions such as: Are the results important? Will researchers or practitioners build on these ideas? Use examples from the guidelines to illustrate strong vs modest significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the tasks or methods are new, whether the work is a novel combination of techniques, and whether it is clear how this work differs from previous contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that related work is adequately cited. If the paper is similar to prior work, explain specific differences. Provide related citations when asserting precedence or lack of novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the ideas will have long-term impact: do they bridge fields or push the community in a new direction? Could techniques be applied more broadly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the methods, proofs, or code could be used in other settings. Suggest release of implementations to increase impact if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical quality (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission is technically sound: are claims well supported by theoretical analysis or empirical results? Is the evaluation sufficient to justify main claims? Are there technical errors or missing assumptions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate concrete technical problems (e.g., incorrect equation, missing assumption) and whether they are typos or substantive flaws. Judge whether the results justify the claims and whether limitations are acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and clarity (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the submission is clearly written and well organized for a reader with appropriate background. Is notation defined? Are sections and the flow logical?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give constructive suggestions for improving clarity (e.g., define variables before use, fix overloaded notation, restructure sections). Note typos, unclear sentences, and formatting issues only after major content issues are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the paper contains enough details to reproduce results. If code or supplementary material is provided and you ran it, note whether you could reproduce results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for details like algorithm descriptions, hyperparameter selection, and dataset descriptions. If essential details (e.g., hyperparameter tuning) are missing, request clarification. Mention whether provided code reproduces the claims if you tested it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct: tone, politeness, and constructive language
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain polite and avoid dismissive phrasing such as 'This paper did not contribute any new ideas.' Instead, try to find at least one contribution and comment on its significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame criticisms constructively, cite specific issues, and propose remedies or experiments authors could run. The review should help authors improve their work even if the recommendation is negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural scoring guidance and batch handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Your numerical/overall recommendation should reflect absolute judgments of contribution quality; do not alter scores to maintain an artificial balance across your assigned papers. Do not assume the set of papers you received is an unbiased sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be consistent across reviews and justify scores in the written justification; use the Detailed Comments to expand on complex points rather than leaving them as unsubstantiated score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and prioritization of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin detailed comments with the most significant issues and put the least significant comments (which can nevertheless be useful) at the end of the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This top-down organization helps authors and meta-reviewers focus on the critical problems first and allows the author response to address the main concerns efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and citation when challenging novelty or prior-art claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If you assert that some aspect of the paper has been done before, you must provide relevant citations to support that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsupported assertions about prior work weaken a review. Give precise references and, when possible, explain how the prior work overlaps and why the submission may or may not be distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of contributions (illustrative list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines provide exemplar contribution statements such as thorough experimental validation, improved sample or computational complexity, robust handling of specific shifts, unifying frameworks, demonstrating limitations of popular approaches, and formulating novel problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these exemplar templates when articulating a paper's merits to make your praise specific and comparable across submissions.
